intervals.label: HAGAR array in regular observation
intervals.note: The date is that of the first regular observations with HAGAR, the first phase of the HIGRO project, not a founding date of the site; MACE followed (regular observations from September 2021).
intervals.quote: Regular source observations are running since September 2008.

name: Hanle Observatory
notes: The HIGRO name is taken from the HAGAR paper ("first phase of the HImalayan Gamma-Ray Observatory (HIGRO) project") and the MACE sensitivity paper.
No operator is recorded: HAGAR was built by TIFR, IIA, BARC and SINP (author affiliations, Astrophys. Space Sci. Trans. 7, 501) and MACE by BARC; no source fetched names one operator of the site.
The Indian Astronomical Observatory (IIA optical telescopes) is also at Hanle; it is a separate facility and is not recorded here.

altitude.quote: set-up at Hanle, at 4270 m amsl

summary.plain: A very high mountain site at Hanle in Ladakh, northern India, home to two Indian gamma-ray telescopes: the HAGAR array and the 21 m MACE telescope. At about 4270 metres it hosts the highest Cherenkov telescopes in the world.
summary.technical: Hanle (Ladakh, Himalayas, 4270 m a.s.l.): the Himalayan Gamma-Ray Observatory (HIGRO) site, hosting the HAGAR wavefront-sampling array (first phase, regular observations since September 2008) and the 21 m MACE imaging Cherenkov telescope.
